recall_prompt: Say the definition of the power set, and give one example together with the number of subsets.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: State the definition
steps.margin_note: First mark. The words "the set of all subsets" and the symbol P(A) are both wanted.
lines: Let A be a set. The set of all subsets of A is called the power set of A, and is written P(A).
In set-builder form, P(A) = {X : X ⊆ A}.
Every power set contains ∅ and A itself, because ∅ ⊆ A and A ⊆ A.

recall.must_convey: That the power set of A is the set of all subsets of A, written P(A).
accept: the power set is the set of all subsets of A
it is written P of A and equals the set of all X such that X is a subset of A
it always contains the empty set and A itself
power set ante A yokka anni subsets tho unna set
its members are subsets, not elements

steps.why: The definition is about subsets, not elements, so every member of P(A) is itself a set. That distinction is the whole of the first mark, and it is what makes {a} ∈ P(A) correct while a ∈ P(A) is wrong.
common_mistakes: Saying P(A) is the set of elements of A.
Writing a ∈ P(A) for an element a of A, when the correct statement is {a} ∈ P(A).
Leaving out the symbol P(A) and giving only words.
steps.memory_tip: Power set means "all the subsets", so its members are sets and are written inside their own braces.

steps.label: Give an example and the count of subsets
steps.margin_note: Second mark. One worked example plus the count 2ⁿ finishes a two-mark definition question.
lines: Take A = {a, b}. Its subsets are ∅, {a}, {b} and {a, b}.
In general, if A is finite with n(A) = n, then n(P(A)) = 2ⁿ.

lines.text: ∴ P(A) = {X : X ⊆ A},  and n(P(A)) = 2ⁿ when n(A) = n

recall.must_convey: That a small example is given, such as A = {a, b} with four subsets, and that a set with n elements has 2 to the power n subsets.
accept: for a set with two elements there are four subsets
P of a b is empty set, a, b and a b
a set with n elements has two to the power n subsets
rendu elements unte naalugu subsets, two power n
give a small example and the count two power n

steps.why: A small example shows at once that the members of P(A) are sets, and it lets the count 2ⁿ be checked on the page instead of being quoted from memory.
common_mistakes: Leaving ∅ or A itself out of the list of subsets.
Choosing an example with so many elements that the list cannot be completed.
steps.memory_tip: Each element is either kept or dropped, so there are 2 choices per element and 2ⁿ subsets in all.
